_help: Edit this file to update the page. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Newest date goes at the top. Image names must match files in the images folder. Topics: Segments, Objects, Bounding boxes, Verbs & actions, Locations, Camera motion, Other field.

items.text: Mark “look down” in camera motion only when the ego looks down at a specific moment.
points: If the ego works while looking down for the entire task, don’t mark “look down” throughout the video. It isn’t a movement, just the ego’s working position.

items.text: An atomic segment holds one verb. If you need two verbs, split the atomic segment into two.
points: Put the first verb in the first atomic segment and the second verb in the next one.
Never add two verbs to a single atomic segment.

items.text: Object indexing restarts in every new coarse segment.
points: Example: if coarse segment 1 has Cloth 1, Cloth 2 and Cloth 3, the cloths in coarse segment 2 start again from Cloth 1, not Cloth 4.
Number objects based only on what is in the current coarse segment.

items.text: When hands are washed under a faucet, label it as below and draw a bounding box around the hand as an object. This is an exception to the usual rule of never boxing hands.
points: Verb: wash
Object: hand
Location: under @faucet

items.text: When using “hold” for objects like brooms or mops, specify the relevant part, such as “handle of”, wherever applicable.
points: Example: Verb: hold · Object: mop · Object description: handle of

items.text: When a video shows multiple clothes piled up on the floor, annotate each piece of clothing as a separate object.
points: Example: if 10–15 pieces of clothing are piled together and the ego picks them up one by one from the top, give each piece its own object ID: Cloth 1, Cloth 2, Cloth 3, and so on.
If all the clothes look identical, with the same color and pattern, you can use the same object description for each one. For example, if all of them are blue, describe each object as “blue cloth”.
This is acceptable only when multiple identical objects of the same type are present.

items.text: Annotate trouser-pulling actions based on whether one leg or both legs are pulled.
points: Leave out the Object description when both trouser legs are pulled together.

items.text: Camera motion can be sequential. Write every movement the ego makes, in the order it happens.
points: Example: if the ego moves forward, turns right, moves forward, turns left and moves forward again, the camera motion is: move forward, turn right, move forward, turn left, move forward

items.text: Capture every camera movement, including minute turns and slight looks. The client expects even light movements to be labelled.
When marking a wall with a bounding box, if you can clearly tell the surfaces apart, draw one bounding box around only the surface the ego is working on.
points: Example: in the attached image, the left and right walls are separated by the staircase. The ego works only on the right wall, so only the right wall is boxed.
Follow this in all upcoming files.

items.text: If a person mops a floor, the verb is now “mops”, not “wipes”.
For “folds” and “unfolds”, mention the location if the object is in contact with any surface.
When a person transfers a cloth from one hand to the other, mark only the cloth as the object, not the hands. You can mention the hand in the location field.
Use body movement and head movement as labels in camera motion.
Annotators are still marking “idle” in the camera motion field. If there is no camera movement, leave the field blank.
Camera movement now includes looking up and down, and looking left and right.
If a person wipes one side of a door and then moves to the other side to wipe it, split the task into two separate coarse segments and label each one with its own atomic actions.
If a cloth is hanging on a hanger mounted on the wall, use the term “ceiling cloth hanger”.
Previously we used “opens the tap”. Now specify the exact part being interacted with: “opens the knob of the faucet”.
If a person transfers a cloth from one hand to the other, mark only the cloth, not the hands.
Residue and dust particles on the floor are now marked as objects, using small bounding boxes.
Don’t mention brand names in object names.
Use the most relevant action name.
For actions on residue and dirt, the location now starts with “from”.
When the left hand holds two objects, mention one object in the verb and location fields and the other in the Other field, separated with a comma ( , ).
Use the verb “pour” only when describing the pouring of liquids.
points: For other solid objects, use verbs such as dispense, spill or move.

items.text: Perform the same continuous action for pick and place. Do not merge the coarse segments.
When the left hand is holding an object and the right hand is not performing any action:
points: Left hand: holding an object
Right hand: idle (no action)

items.text: When marking the floor or wall with a bounding box, mark the entire relevant area.
points: Example: if the hall, kitchen and bedroom floors are visible but the action takes place in the hall, box the entire hall floor only. Don’t include the kitchen or bedroom.

items.text: Wiping the hands with a towel: Verb is idle.
“Bends down” and “rises up” can now be included in camera motion labels.
Bounding boxes need to be marked correctly.

mistakes.title: Boxes not drawn on the first visible frame
mistakes.details: In coarse segments, bounding boxes are not consistently drawn on the first frame where the object becomes visible.

mistakes.title: Using “idle” in camera motion
mistakes.details: Annotators are still entering “idle” in the Camera motion field. If there is no camera movement, leave the field blank.

mistakes.title: Confusing similar objects and verbs
mistakes.details: Similar objects (shelf / cabinet / rack, mop / brush / wiper) and similar action verbs (clean / wipe / sweep) are being mixed up. Use the name that matches what you see in the video.

mistakes.title: Using “rest on” for a resting hand
mistakes.details: Don’t use “rest on” when a hand is resting on an object. Use “idle” instead.

mistakes.title: Inconsistent camera motion labels
mistakes.details: Camera movements are not being labeled consistently or accurately across tasks. Always mention camera movements, even when the movement is slight.
